title: hipDNN UED
description: Universal Engine Descriptor. Implements RFC 0020 section 4.2 and the RFC 0021 slot members ('slots', 'shared_workspace', version 1.1). It differs from the RFC's inline schema as RFC 0020 section 4.2 lists: 'revision' is an optional '<major>.<minor>' authored revision; keys starting with 'x-' or '_', and the key 'provenance', are extensions the loader ignores; 'nodes' holds at most 32 items (section 4.3.2); and the RFC 0021 members, the version enum and the slot rules below. Structural shape only; registry and cross-reference rules are semantic (section 13.2).

allOf.description: RFC 0021 section 4: a slotted engine declares 'metadata', 'sort_kernel_catalog', 'knobs' and 'predict_applicable_kernels' per slot, never on the engine, and needs format 1.1. An unslotted engine carries 'metadata'.
RFC 0021 section 6: 'shared_workspace' needs 'slots' and a native graph_match, which publishes the token.

uhd_ids.description: One UHD id, or a non-empty list of distinct ids with at most one per ranking metric (the metric rule is semantic; see RFC 0019 section 3.1).

revision.description: Authored revision as '<major>.<minor>'; defaults to 1.0 when absent. Independent of 'version', which gates the file format.

id.description: This descriptor's own UUID. Unique across loaded UEDs except for content-identical duplicates (semantic; see RFC 0020 section 13.2.1).

sdk_version.description: hipDNN graph schema version this pattern was authored against, as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (unsigned decimal integers that fit a 32-bit int) with an optional '.TWEAK' of ASCII letters and digits that the loader ignores; defaults to the engine plugin API baseline when absent.

sort_kernel_catalog.description: Arch -> UHD id, or a list of UHD ids with at most one per ranking metric (RFC 0019 section 3.1). Kernel-selection heuristics; each id MUST resolve to a loadable UHD (semantic; see RFC 0020 section 13.2).

predict_engine.description: Arch -> UHD id, or a list of UHD ids with at most one per ranking metric (RFC 0019 section 3.1). Optional engine-level estimates; each id MUST resolve to a loadable UHD (semantic; see RFC 0020 section 13.2).

predict_applicable_kernels.description: Arch -> UHD id. Optional candidate generator; each value MUST resolve to a loadable UHD (semantic; see RFC 0020 section 13.2).

metadata.description: Cross-reference: MUST resolve to a loadable KMD (semantic; see RFC 0020 section 13.2). Required on an unslotted engine; a slotted one declares it per slot.

knobs.description: Each entry MUST be a field name declared by the referenced KMD (semantic; see RFC 0020 section 13.2).

slots.description: RFC 0021 section 4: the engine's kernel program, in launch order. Each slot carries the selection members an unslotted engine carries itself. Slot names are unique within the engine (semantic).

metadata.description: Cross-reference: MUST resolve to a loadable KMD (semantic).

sort_kernel_catalog.description: Arch -> UHD id, or a list of UHD ids. The slot's metric-less ranker (RFC 0021 section 7).

knobs.description: Each entry MUST be a field name declared by the slot's KMD (semantic).

shared_workspace.description: RFC 0021 section 6: the bound token holding the size of the workspace region every slot shares.

graph_match.description: Stage one: exactly one arm. 'nodes' is the declarative pattern (RFC 0020 section 4.3); 'native' names a C++ function the provider registers (section 4.5) and MUST be registered in the provider's graph-match registry (semantic; see section 13.2).

nodes.description: Structural pattern over the op DAG. Opcodes, operand and result names MUST resolve against the op-schema registry (semantic; see RFC 0020 section 13.2).

id.description: Attributes namespace root; unique within 'nodes', not 'graph', 'kernel' or 'device', and not a pattern variable name. The loader checks these rules when it parses the pattern; this schema does not.

operands.description: Operand name the op declares -> pattern variable. '?' marks an operand the registry declares optional (semantic).

results.description: Result name the op declares -> pattern variable. A result is always produced, so it takes no '?'.
